title: Daily Dose #348: Be Still Before God
body:
**“Be still, and know that I am God.”**

Psalm 46 is not describing a naturally peaceful world. The earth gives way, mountains move, nations rage and kingdoms totter. In the middle of that noise, God says, “Be still.”

This is not a vague invitation to empty the mind. It is a command to stop striving and recognise the Lord’s authority. He will be exalted. The chaos does not remove Him from His throne.

Our lives can be loud even in a quiet room. The mind rehearses conversations, imagines outcomes and tries to solve tomorrow before today has finished. Activity can become a way of avoiding dependence.

Take a few minutes and become still before God. Put the phone down. Name what is troubling you. Read this psalm slowly. You do not need to deny the problem, but you do need to remember that the problem is not God.

Stillness will not answer every question. It places every question beneath the God who still rules, even when life feels out of control.

**Remember:** Peace grows when control is surrendered.
